question.text: Due Date Rate (DDR) / Final Settlement Price (FSP) in commodity futures is used for:

answer.text: Final settlement price, delivery default penalty, delivery or payment obligations, and buyer compensation in case of non-delivery
Setting the initial margin for new positions

explanation.text: The Logic: The source distinguishes the Daily Settlement Price (DSP), used for daily mark-to-market profit or loss, from the Final Settlement Price (FSP)/Due Date Rate (DDR), which is used for final settlement, delivery default penalty, delivery or payment obligations, and compensation to buyers. The Trap: Initial margin uses VaR methodology. Brokerage and membership fees are separate. Daily MTM is the DSP role, not the DDR/FSP role. Note: Keep DSP and DDR/FSP distinct: DSP handles daily MTM; DDR/FSP handles final settlement and delivery-related obligations.
